article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 60% Sativa / 40% Indica
Genetics: Lemon Skunk × Super Silver Haze
Breeder: The Bulldog Seeds
THC Content: 19–23%
CBD Content: Generally low
Terpene Profile: limonene , myrcene , alpha-pinene
Primary Flavors: Lemon, citrus peel, pine, spice, skunk
Flowering Time (Indoor): 10–11 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: 600–700 grams per square meter
Outdoor Yield: High
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Bulldog Haze belongs to the period when Amsterdam cannabis breeding was still heavily influenced by Haze , Skunk , Northern Lights , and sharp citrus genetics rather than the dessert-heavy families that dominate many modern menus. Named for Amsterdam’s famous Bulldog brand, the cultivar combines the acidic lemon character of Lemon Skunk with the long-lasting cerebral intensity of Super Silver Haze. The resulting weed is pungent without being one-dimensional: fresh lemon and pine appear immediately, but spice, old-school skunk, wood, and a faint earthy sweetness emerge underneath. Its effects follow a similarly layered path, beginning with an alert cerebral rush before settling into a more grounded physical calm.
Genetics and Lineage

The Bulldog Seeds created Bulldog Haze by crossing Lemon Skunk with Super Silver Haze. Historical Bulldog seed descriptions characterize the pairing as an attempt to combine Super Silver Haze’s potency and classic Haze flavor with the pungent citrus qualities of Lemon Skunk. The cultivar is generally classified around 60% sativa and 40% indica, although the long flowering cycle and energetic early effect clearly reveal the Haze side of its ancestry.

Its parental genetics provide considerably more depth than the two-name pedigree suggests. Green House Seed Company currently identifies Lemon Skunk as Skunk × Citral. The parent finishes much faster than most Haze lines and brings intense citrus aroma, branching growth, and a combination of cerebral and physical effects. Super Silver Haze, meanwhile, is officially listed as Skunk × Northern Lights × Haze and remains one of Green House’s best-known sativa-dominant cultivars. It earned consecutive High Times Cannabis Cup victories in 1997, 1998, and 1999 and is recognized for pine, wood, Haze aromatics, substantial stretch, and a powerful long-lasting high.

Crossing those parents gives Bulldog Haze an unmistakably old-school genetic identity. Skunk appears on both sides of the family tree, providing vigor, pungency, and flower density, while Citral contributes lemon character. Northern Lights introduces a heavier physical component and improved flower formation, and Haze pushes the hybrid toward taller growth, longer flowering, and pronounced cerebral effects. Rather than disguising those influences beneath excessive sweetness, the finished cannabis expresses them directly.
Effects and Experience

The onset can arrive quickly. A noticeable lift behind the eyes is often followed by increased mental activity, a brighter mood, and greater interest in whatever is happening nearby. Conversation may become easier, music can seem more detailed, and routine activities can acquire an extra layer of novelty. This is not generally the dreamy, disconnected type of marijuana high associated with heavy evening indicas. At moderate amounts, Bulldog Haze leans toward alertness, sociability, and mental stimulation.

As the experience develops, the Lemon Skunk and Northern Lights influence becomes easier to recognize. Physical tension may ease without eliminating the cerebral energy, producing a middle stage that combines mental activity with a calmer body. That balance helps explain why the strain has historically appealed to Haze enthusiasts who want strong cerebral effects without the thin or jittery character some highly sativa-leaning cultivars can produce. The high can also be unusually persistent, reflecting Super Silver Haze’s reputation for long duration.

Dose strongly affects where the experience ends. More substantial consumption can transform an energetic session into something considerably heavier, while sensitive consumers may encounter restlessness, dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, or anxious thinking. THC concentrations around 20% are potent enough that people without an established tolerance should approach the weed conservatively.
Medical Benefits

Some medical marijuana consumers favor sativa-dominant hybrids when fatigue, low mood, or daytime stress makes a heavily sedating cultivar undesirable. Bulldog Haze’s initial combination of mood elevation and mental stimulation may fit that preference, while the physical relaxation developing later can make the experience feel less sharply stimulating than a pure Haze. Anecdotally, similar THC-dominant cannabis is also chosen by people seeking temporary relief from appetite loss, nausea, tension, or certain forms of discomfort.

Specific therapeutic claims require considerably more caution. Bulldog Haze itself has not been established through controlled clinical trials as a treatment for depression, anxiety, ADHD, chronic pain , migraine, or other medical conditions. Cannabis strain names do not represent standardized pharmaceutical formulations, and cannabinoid concentrations can differ materially between two harvests carrying the same label.

Its relatively high THC level is particularly important for patients to consider. THC may provide therapeutic benefit in some contexts, yet increasing the dose can also increase cognitive impairment, dizziness, anxiety, and sedation. Anyone combining marijuana with prescription medication or using cannabis for a significant medical condition should evaluate the chemistry of the actual product rather than relying solely on the strain’s reputation.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Lemon dominates the first encounter with properly cured Bulldog Haze flower. Rather than soft lemon candy, the scent is closer to fresh peel, citrus oil, and sharp zest. Pine and woody Haze notes sit directly underneath, while opening the flower releases stronger skunk, herbs, and pepper. The aroma can become quite pungent once ground, carrying the penetrating quality expected from a genetic background that contains Skunk on both sides.

Flavor retains the citrus character but broadens considerably after inhalation. Lemon appears first, followed by fresh pine and herbs through the middle. Spice and an old-school Haze earthiness become more noticeable on the exhale, sometimes accompanied by a faint metallic or incense-like quality inherited from Super Silver Haze. Green House describes that parent as expressing myrcene, D-limonene, and alpha-pinene, which corresponds closely with the woody, citrus, and pine qualities found throughout this family.

Actual terpene content should always be confirmed through laboratory testing when available. Cultivation environment, phenotype, nutrition, harvest timing, drying, and storage can all alter the aromatic profile. One batch may emphasize lemon and pine, while another can lean much more strongly toward skunk, spice, or woody incense.
Growing Information

Bulldog Haze carries the growth habits expected from its Haze ancestry. Plants can stretch appreciably after flowering begins, and branches may develop enough distance between nodes that canopy management becomes useful indoors. The cultivar normally requires approximately 10–11 weeks of flowering, considerably longer than compact indica hybrids but typical for a Super Silver Haze descendant. Historical Bulldog material describes the strain as a feminized photoperiod variety suited to both indoor and outdoor cultivation.

Indoor yield potential is one of its more attractive traits. Historical figures commonly place production around 600–700 grams per square meter under optimized conditions. Those numbers should be understood as breeder-era potential rather than guaranteed harvests. Lighting intensity, root space, phenotype, temperature, plant health, and canopy management can create very large differences between gardens.

Outdoor growers need enough season for the lengthy bloom cycle to finish. October is the typical harvest period in the Northern Hemisphere, making warm temperate, Mediterranean, subtropical, and similarly long-season climates the most natural fit. Super Silver Haze itself is known for vigorous stretch and can become extremely large outdoors, so Bulldog Haze should not be treated like a compact patio indica. Good spacing and airflow become increasingly important as flower mass increases toward harvest.
FAQ
Is Bulldog Haze indica or sativa?

Bulldog Haze is a sativa-dominant hybrid, generally described as approximately 60% sativa and 40% indica. Its early effects emphasize cerebral energy and mood elevation, while a calmer physical component becomes more apparent later.
What are the genetics of Bulldog Haze?

The original The Bulldog Seeds cultivar is Lemon Skunk × Super Silver Haze. Lemon Skunk itself is Skunk × Citral, while Super Silver Haze combines Skunk, Northern Lights, and Haze genetics. This places several foundational Dutch cannabis lines within the strain’s extended pedigree.
How strong is Bulldog Haze?

Historical descriptions place THC around 19.38%, while commercial examples are frequently reported in roughly the 19–23% range. Actual potency depends on phenotype and cultivation, so laboratory testing for the specific batch is more meaningful than a universal strain percentage.
What does Bulldog Haze taste like?

Lemon and citrus dominate, followed by pine, spice, herbs, wood, and classic skunk. Certain flowers develop a more pronounced incense-like Haze character on the exhale, while others emphasize the sharper Lemon Skunk side of the lineage.
How long does Bulldog Haze take to flower?

Indoor flowering normally requires approximately 10–11 weeks, or around 70–77 days. Historical strain records frequently place the average close to 74 days. Outdoors, plants generally reach maturity during October where the climate provides a sufficiently long growing season.
Final Thoughts on Bulldog Haze

Bulldog Haze captures a particular chapter of Amsterdam marijuana breeding in which recognizable Haze and Skunk character mattered more than chasing extreme sweetness or exotic strain names. Lemon Skunk supplies bright citrus and additional vigor, while Super Silver Haze brings the long cerebral high, pine, wood, and unmistakable Haze structure. The cross preserves enough physical weight to keep the experience balanced without erasing the energetic personality that defines the cultivar.

For cannabis enthusiasts interested in classic Dutch genetics, its appeal extends beyond nostalgia. The flower offers a sharply defined lemon-pine profile, substantial potency, long-lasting effects, and strong production potential from plants given enough time to finish properly. Bulldog Haze may require more patience than an eight-week modern hybrid, but its combination of citrus, spice, skunk, and cerebral intensity gives the strain an identity that remains distinctly its own.
